gaps.sentence: The box was heavy enough ___ two people.
gaps.explanation: adjective + enough + to-infinitive: heavy enough to need.

gaps.sentence: I could hear the neighbours ___ again last night.
gaps.explanation: hear + object + -ing = hear an action in progress: hear them arguing.

gaps.sentence: She couldn't resist ___ the last biscuit.
The rules don't ___ visitors to touch the paintings.
gaps.explanation: allow + object + to-infinitive: allow visitors to touch. (let + bare: let visitors touch.)

gaps.sentence: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.
gaps.explanation: 'to' is a preposition in look forward to, so -ing follows: hearing.

gaps.sentence: They agreed ___ the deadline by a week.
gaps.explanation: 'Agree to do something' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.
